[element-notes]
=== `<notes>` Notes Section

A container element to hold the notes that may appear within the front matter (<<element-front,`<front>`>>) or in the rear matter (<<element-back,`<back>`>>) of a standards document or adoption document.

#### Usage/Remarks
The Notes Section (<<element-notes,`<notes>`>>) is a section-like grouping of material that can be used in the front or back matter of a standard to hold normative or non-normative notes, groups of such notes (<<element-notes-group,`<notes-group>`>>), normative or non-normative examples, or even paragraphs and sections of prose. Typical use is to hold normative and non-normative notes in the front matter (<<element-front,`<front>`>> or <<element-adoption-front,`<adoption-front>`>>) of a standards document.

#### Related Elements

This Tag Set contains several elements that are notes or may be used to group notes: <<element-normative-note,`<normative-note>`>> A note with normative content that can be part of the narrative text or inside one of the notes grouping elements in the body text, front matter, or back matter of a standard or adoption. <<element-non-normative-note,`<non-normative-note>`>> A note with non-normative content that can be part of the narrative text or inside one of the notes grouping elements in the body text, front matter, or back matter of a standard or adoption. <<element-notes,`<notes>`>> A section containing notes that may appear in the front or back matter of a standard or adoption. <<element-notes-group,`<notes-group>`>> A headed (titled) group of normative or non-normative notes and examples within the narrative body of a standard or adoption. <<element-meta-note,`<meta-note>`>> A note within the metadata of a standards or adoption document, as opposed to the other note types that occur within the front matter, body, or back matter of a document.

##### Notes in the front matter

....
...
<front>
 <std-meta>...</std-meta>
 <notes>
  <p><bold>Notice and Disclaimer of Liability Concerning 
   the Use of IEEE Documents:</bold> IEEE Standards 
   documents are developed within the IEEE Societies and 
   the Standards Coordinating Committees of the IEEE 
   Standards Association (IEEE-SA) Standards Board. IEEE 
   develops its standards ...</p>
  ...
 </notes>
</front>
...
